machines/solar-tracker.title: Solar Tracker (L)
machines/solar-tracker.description: Supply nearby machines with up to 16 kW in sunlight. The built-in battery stores energy for darkness; it does not increase peak generation.

tdk.title: Solar Tracker (L) — Moon Sweepers Specs & Setup
tdk.description: Supply nearby machines with up to 16 kW in sunlight. The built-in battery stores energy for darkness; it does not increase peak generation in Moon Sweepers.

sectionsOverride.heading: Output and wireless range
paragraphs: The $300 Solar Tracker follows the Sun, generates up to 16 kW and supplies machines within 34 m. Its 10 kWh battery stores energy for lower-generation periods.

sectionsOverride.heading: Choose the connected machines
paragraphs: One Tracker can cover a 10 kW chamber in enough sunlight. It cannot cover an 18 kW press at nominal demand by itself. Add the load of every running machine within the powered area.

sectionsOverride.heading: Store enough for night
paragraphs: At an ideal 10 kW load, a full 10 kWh battery represents one hour of energy. Actual uptime depends on charging, sunlight, available output and other machines. Peak generation is not an all-day average.

machines/solar-post.title: Solar Post (S)
machines/solar-post.description: A compact $75 solar panel with 3 kW peak output. Check the Sun’s direction and keep consumers within its 16 m range.

tdk.title: Solar Post (S) — Moon Sweepers Specs & Setup
tdk.description: Check the Moon Sweepers Solar Post’s $75 price, 3 kW peak output and 16 m range. Plan fixed-panel placement and understand why it cannot store night power.

sectionsOverride.heading: Where the small panel fits
paragraphs: The $75 Solar Post supplies up to 3 kW within 16 m. It has no listed battery, so it cannot keep a powered processor running through darkness on its own.

sectionsOverride.heading: Positioning and load
paragraphs: Face this fixed panel toward the Sun. A 10 kW chamber needs more than one small panel even at peak output. Compare total generation with the connected load.

sectionsOverride.heading: Expanding a daytime supply
paragraphs: Use the small panel where its range and daytime output are enough. For continuous production, compare larger panels and their stored energy before building a dense group of small panels.

machines/solar-twin.title: Solar Twin (M)
machines/solar-twin.description: Supply up to 7.5 kW and store 4 kWh for later. Position the panel toward the Sun and check the load across its 24 m range.

tdk.title: Solar Twin (M) — Moon Sweepers Specs & Setup
tdk.description: Compare the Moon Sweepers Solar Twin’s 7.5 kW output, 4 kWh battery and 24 m range. Check the $150 price and plan your connected load through changing light.

sectionsOverride.heading: Generation and storage
paragraphs: The $150 Solar Twin supplies up to 7.5 kW within 24 m and stores 4 kWh. Battery capacity is energy held for later, not extra peak generation.

sectionsOverride.heading: Keep the panel facing sunlight
paragraphs: This model does not track the Sun. Placement affects how much daylight power it collects. Its peak output is below a chamber’s 10 kW nominal demand.

sectionsOverride.heading: Plan the dark period
paragraphs: At an ideal 10 kW load, 4 kWh represents 24 minutes of energy. This is a capacity calculation, not a guarantee that the panel alone supplies the load. Include other machines and charging conditions.

faqs.answer: A $25 Household Broom increases base capacity to 3 kg. Its first $30 container doubles that capacity. Compare those upgrades with a belt-fed route based on how often you return to the station.

faqs.question: Is stone always the best income route?
faqs.answer: Stone has the highest base price per kilogram, but production needs dust and sand, enough power and clear delivery belts. Compare the extra value with the whole build cost and sustainable supply.

faqs.question: Should the crew buy the same tool twice?
faqs.answer: Hand tools are personal purchases, while the host’s matrix is shared. Agree who collects, transports and builds before spending the wallet on duplicate equipment.

faqs.question: Can one belt feed two chambers and five presses?
faqs.answer: Not at the full recipe rate with 1 kg capsules. The line needs 100 kg/min of raw dust, while ideal belt spacing carries 88 capsules/min. Use additional feeds or expect reduced uptime.

faqs.question: Why do capsules stop despite a full source?
faqs.answer: Find the first stopped capsule. A reversed belt, missing connection, full receiver or blocked output can hold up everything upstream. Also check ingredients and power at processors.

faqs.question: Who keeps a co-op world?
faqs.answer: The host’s save slot holds the world. Purchases use shared money, but vehicles belong to their buyer. Back up the host’s slot before attempting recovery.

faqs.answer: No. It transfers hand-tool dust into capsules. Connect its output to a station intake to sell, or to processing equipment to make sand and stone.

faqs.question: Does a Merger double outgoing capacity?
faqs.answer: No. Both feeds share one exit. If they exceed its capacity, the queue grows even when each source works correctly alone.

guides/pressure-chamber-guide.title: Pressure Chamber Recipe & Power Guide
guides/pressure-chamber-guide.description: Supply dust and power to make sand. Compare full batches, partial loads and the value gained before adding a Stone Press.

tdk.title: Pressure Chamber Guide — Moon Sweepers Guide
tdk.description: Set up a Pressure Chamber in Moon Sweepers with dust, power and a clear sand output. Compare full batches, partial loads and the extra value of processing.

faqs.question: Does processing triple the weight of dust?
faqs.answer: No. A full 5 kg dust batch becomes 5 kg sand. Base value rises from $1/kg to $3/kg; the mass stays the same.

Check generation and range: A 16 kW peak Tracker can cover a 10 kW chamber in enough sunlight. Keep the chamber within wireless range and check other connected machines. For night operation, budget stored energy separately from daytime generation.

guides/stone-press-guide.title: How the Stone Press Works

faqs.question: Can I feed only sand to the press?
faqs.answer: No. Each full cycle needs 1 kg raw dust and 1 kg sand for one 2 kg block. Keep an unprocessed dust branch beside the chamber’s output.

guides/solar-power-guide.title: Solar Power, Battery & Night Planning

faqs.question: Can one Tracker power a Stone Press?
faqs.answer: Its peak 16 kW output is below the press’s nominal 18 kW demand. Add generation, then budget stored energy for darkness.

Keep runtime claims conditional: Compare the running load in kW with the stored energy in kWh. Observe the battery after sunrise and before sunset to see whether daytime generation replenishes what your machines use overnight. A slow processor also needs its input checked before you add panels.

faqs.question: Why is Joonas waiting with a full bin?
faqs.answer: Check that a catcher exists, has receiving space and can drain. Catchers within 100 m form groups; receiving capacity affects which group the robot chooses.

Plan the receiving network first: Budget $20,000 for J.O.O.N.A.S. and $1,500 for each catcher before belts and other equipment. This robot selects dusty sectors across the Moon, while Mk I and Mk II vacuums work near their docks. Plan its receiver capacity around actual deliveries.

faqs.question: Do containers stack with Dust Compactor?
faqs.answer: Yes. Apply the container level multiplier and then Dust Compactor’s modifier. Compare the combined capacity rather than adding percentages to the base.

faqs.answer: No. It speeds vehicle unloading. The garage silo and exit belts still need capacity to carry the delivered material away.

faqs.answer: Do not assume an older build opens a newer save. Patch 1.0.4 documents older-build incompatibility. Copy originals and backups before checking a restore.

faqs.question: How do kW and kWh compare?
faqs.answer: Multiply load in kW by running time in hours to get an ideal kWh budget. Account separately for charging limits, available output and losses.

Test the complete cycle: Look at stored energy after sunrise, near midday and before sunset. If the battery drains before morning, add generation in range, reduce simultaneous processing or let part of the line idle at night. Recheck the next cycle after changing the load.
